title: Threshold closure, clock no-go models, complete-frame pair inertia, and a normalized two-scale certificate

claims.statement: For 1 <= kappa < 2, no scalar rank-trace threshold c > 0 and no nonnegative mixture of such threshold certificates improves the simple-zero lower bound 2-kappa; c=2 is optimal.
At complete-frame level, changing only the sampling-grid phase preserves the atom Gram kernel by the bilinear Poisson identity.

Every fixed finite direct sum or nonnegative mixture of same-scale tapers is Gram-equivalent to one effective taper, and fixed-width plateau tapers admit an asymptotically sharp 2/3-simple, 5/6-distinct clock-multiplicity model.

In the ideal integer-occupancy model with reference density theta and relative scale alpha, the simple-cell proportion is at least theta-(1-theta)^2/theta-alpha*theta/(3*omega_alpha)-epsilon/omega_alpha, where omega_alpha=(2alpha-1)/alpha^2. The optimal relative scale is alpha=3/4.

At relative scale 3/4, the ideal two-scale bound exceeds the same-scale Zeta23 H(theta) certificate by exactly 5*theta/96-(9/8)*epsilon; epsilon<5*theta/108 preserves a strict gain. The theta->1 zero-error limit is 23/32.
At theta=1 and relative scale 3/4, every arrangement of the 0/1/2 Nyquist extremal occupancy distribution incurs the exact ideal second-moment excess 5/108 over the Zeta23 prime-side constant.
For an isolated aligned off-line reflection pair in the ideal centered box model, the c=2 defect is 2*((sinh(a)/a)^2-1), at least (2/3)*a^2, and contracts by at most lambda^2 under scale restriction.
Abstract hyperbolic pair blocks can cancel their negative directions exactly, so scalar per-scale trace, Frobenius and inertia data do not recover individual pair depth.

For a real even taper nonzero on an interval, complete analysis vectors at finitely many distinct complex frequencies are linearly independent; consequently p distinct off-line reflection pairs produce a complete pair form with exact inertia (p,p). A full-column-rank finite section has the same inertia.

If the pair synthesis Gram matrix satisfies U_d^*U_d >= A I and the minimum pair multiplicity is m_min, then the finite pair form has ||Q_{d,-}||_F^2 >= p*A^2*m_min^2; divided-difference coordinates isolate a quadratic horizontal-depth coefficient.

validation.expected: all threshold, symbol, normalized occupancy, exact-fraction, finite-circulant, clock, taper-scaling, isolated-pair and abstract cancellation checks PASS

next_frontier: Prove a critical-lattice extraction and finite-section pair-stability theorem that isolates the on-line short-scale quadratic form and keeps total normalized loss below the fixed-theta budget (-27*theta^2+128*theta-96)/(108*theta), or construct an admissible countermodel showing that the current Zeta23 observables cannot meet that budget.
cannot_imply: This attempt does not improve any unconditional zeta-zero proportion.
The ideal 23/32 limit is not a theorem about actual zeta zeros.
The full Frobenius bound for an indefinite P+Q matrix does not automatically upper-bound the on-line PSD block P.
The complete-frame inertia theorem does not provide a uniform lower Riesz bound for the growing finite sections used in Zeta23.
Deterministic computations do not prove the missing extraction, taper, off-line, finite-section or seam estimates.
The parent A-RH-RTD-0001 defect decomposition remains unverified while Issue #25 is open.
This attempt does not prove or refute the Riemann hypothesis.
No claim is repository-verified before an isolated independent-verifier run returns PASS on frozen artifact hashes.
